exact_statement: For every Boolean F on two independent uniform physical address bits X and arbitrarily many uniform data bits Y, if each nonzero conditional squared Fourier row is a coordinate-product law with at most one nonfair varying coordinate, arbitrary nonfair marginal, arbitrary Fourier signs and arbitrary fixed frequency coordinates, then H(S_Y|S_X)<=[3/2+(5/2)h2(1/10)]I_Y(F), sharply, and H(F)<=[6+2log2(65/64)]I(F). If all nonfair primitive magnitude ratios belong to {2,3,4}, the sharper bound H(F)<=[10-3log2(3)]I(F) holds. Universally for every two-address Boolean F, H(w)<=sum_J w_J H_{1/2}(p_J)+2I_X(F); hence full H(F)<=sum_J w_J[H(p_J)+H_{1/2}(p_J)]+2I_X(F). For integer height-two rows of the fixed-ratio family, ratio2 requires at least one other fair coordinate, ratio4 requires at least three, and weights are <=5/8 for ratio2 or3 and <=17/32 for ratio4. Quadratic branch signs admit exactly the equal/overlapping/disjoint affine inverse-support amplitude classification in DERIVATION.md; the low-dimensional exclusion holds for arbitrary signs.
